title: Company Settlement Schedule: Total Loss Tests, Sales Tax and Title Fees by Garaging State
content:
For the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), the garaging state of the owner term selects the total loss test, the motor vehicle sales or title tax rate added to a total loss settlement, and the title transfer fee reimbursed in it. Title fees follow the company's settlement schedule. All six deductible packages carry the same state figures.

| Garaging state | Total loss test | Sales or title tax rate (percent of ACV) | Title transfer fee (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Florida | Repair estimate at least 80 percent of the actual cash value | 6.0 | 77.75 |
| Virginia | Repair estimate at least 75 percent of the actual cash value | 4.15 | 15.0 |
| Texas | Repair estimate at least 100 percent of the actual cash value | 6.25 | 33.0 |
| Georgia | Repair estimate plus salvage value at least the actual cash value | 7.0 | 18.0 |
| Arizona | Repair estimate plus salvage value at least the actual cash value | 5.6 | 4.0 |
| Ohio | Repair estimate plus salvage value at least the actual cash value | 5.75 | 15.0 |

### Further settlement terms, the same in every package

- **Actual cash value.** It is set as the average of two comparable-vehicle valuation reports, adjusted for mileage and condition.
- **Owner-retained salvage.** Allowed: the named insured may keep a total-loss vehicle, and its salvage value is deducted.
- **Loss payee paid first.** Yes: a total loss payment goes first to the listed loss payee, up to the payoff amount.
  - **Governing rule for a total loss of a vehicle with a loss payee.** For a total loss of a vehicle whose coverage lists a loss payee, and only for such a loss, the vehicle value the loss-payee settlement rule sets out is paid in full to the loss payee, which applies it to its payoff and returns any excess to the named insured, while the sales tax and the title fee are paid to the named insured as the owner's tax-and-title payment under its own rule; a total loss of a vehicle with no loss payee remains settled as the actual cash value less the deductible, plus the garaging state's sales tax percent of the actual cash value and its title fee, less the salvage value when the named insured keeps the vehicle, all paid to the named insured.
- **Theft waiting period.** An unrecovered vehicle is settled as a total loss 30 calendar days after the theft is reported.

### How the two kinds of test compare (hypothetical figures)

Take an actual cash value of 9,000.00 USD, a repair estimate of 6,900.00 USD and a salvage value of 2,300.00 USD.
- Under the Florida test (80 percent, which is 7,200.00 USD), this is not a total loss.
- Under the Georgia, Arizona and Ohio test, repair estimate plus salvage value is 9,200.00 USD. That reaches the actual cash value, so the test is met.
